title: Blocking a Channel Is Not Silence

scenes.tts: Three families in northern Pakistan had members who had never experienced pain. The cause was two broken copies of one sodium channel gene, S C N nine A. That gene makes the channel N A V one point seven. In cultured cells, the mutant channels passed no current above background. Lose this channel, lose pain.

scenes.tts: Nociceptor spikes draw on three sodium channels. N A V one point seven, one point eight, and one point nine. A selective blocker of N A V one point seven did not significantly beat placebo in one trial of painful diabetic neuropathy. The drug approved in the United States in January twenty twenty five blocks N A V one point eight instead.
scenes.caption: Nociceptor spikes draw on three sodium channels: Nav1.7, Nav1.8, and Nav1.9. A selective blocker of Nav1.7 did not significantly beat placebo in one trial of painful diabetic neuropathy. The drug approved in the United States in January 2025 blocks Nav1.8 instead.
scenes.visual: A nociceptor ending with a membrane bar and three channel chips; Nav1.7 chip gets a 'no significant gain vs placebo' tag; Nav1.8 chip gets a blocker and 'approved January 2025' tag.

scenes.tts: Now, how is a blocker described? Take human N A V one point eight, expressed in a cell line. A fitted curve links the drug concentration to the current that remains. Half the current remains at one concentration, called K d. In this fit, K d is zero point three eight nanomolar, at thirty seven degrees.
scenes.caption: Now, how is a blocker described? Take human Nav1.8, expressed in a cell line. A fitted curve links the drug concentration to the current that remains. Half the current remains at one concentration, called Kd. In this fit, Kd is 0.38 nM, at 37 °C.
scenes.visual: Axes: concentration (nM, log) against fraction of maximal current; curve drawn from f = 1/(1+C/Kd); Kd marked at 50%.
scenes.narration: Now, how is a blocker described? Take human Nav1.8, expressed in a cell line. A fitted curve links the drug concentration to the current that remains. Half the current remains at one concentration, called Kd. In this fit, Kd is 0.38 nM, at 37 °C.

scenes.tts: Put in numbers. The fraction left is K d over K d plus the concentration. At ten nanomolar, that leaves three point six six percent of the current. To reach ninety nine percent block, the concentration must be thirty seven point six two nanomolar.
scenes.caption: Put in numbers. The fraction left is Kd over Kd plus the concentration. At 10 nM, that leaves 3.66% of the current. To reach 99% block, the concentration must be 37.62 nM.
scenes.visual: On the same curve: a point at 10 nM reading 3.66% left, then a point at 37.62 nM reading 1% left (99% block); the formula shown beside.
scenes.narration: Put in numbers. The fraction left is Kd over Kd plus the concentration. At 10 nM, that leaves 3.66% of the current. To reach 99% block, the concentration must be 37.62 nM.

scenes.tts: Now ask the neuron. In dissociated sensory neurons from adult human organ donors, recorded at thirty seven degrees, the blocker generally reduced repetitive firing, but did not eliminate it. At ten nanomolar, it lowered the spike peak and the shoulder. It largely spared threshold and the initial upstroke.
scenes.caption: Now ask the neuron. In dissociated sensory neurons from adult human organ donors, recorded at 37 °C, the blocker generally reduced repetitive firing, but did not eliminate it. At 10 nM, it lowered the spike peak and the shoulder. It largely spared threshold and the initial upstroke.
scenes.visual: Sketch traces in relative units, labelled 'in this sketch': a spike train before and a smaller, sparser but still present train after; overlay of one spike before/after with peak and shoulder lowered, threshold and upstroke the same.
scenes.narration: Now ask the neuron. In dissociated sensory neurons from adult human organ donors, recorded at 37 °C, the blocker generally reduced repetitive firing, but did not eliminate it. At 10 nM, it lowered the spike peak and the shoulder. It largely spared threshold and the initial upstroke.

scenes.tts: Why does the neuron still fire? The authors' voltage clamp analysis suggested two possible reasons. Many neurons carry such large N A V one point eight currents that even ninety nine percent block leaves nanoampere level current. And N A V one point seven current dominates the initial spikes in these recordings. It could also contribute to repetitive firing. A channel calculation is not neuronal silence. It is certainly not a dose.

A tag marks both as the authors' two possible reasons; Nav1.7 'could also contribute to repetitive firing'.
